title: Three Teams, 18 Points Each: SRH's 55-Run Rout of RCB Sets Up the Tightest Playoff Race in IPL History
excerpt: Ishan Kishan's blistering 79 powers Sunrisers to 255/4 as Hyderabad, Gujarat and Bengaluru finish level — net run rate the only separator
body:
When the scoreboard at the Rajiv Gandhi International Stadium finally settled on Friday evening, it confirmed something IPL fans have never witnessed in 18 previous editions: three teams finishing level on 18 points at the top of the table, with net run rate alone separating first from third.

Sunrisers Hyderabad's emphatic 55-run demolition of Royal Challengers Bengaluru in Match 67 completed a remarkable final-week surge for the hosts. SRH posted a formidable 255/4 — their third-highest total this season — before restricting RCB to 200/4 in reply. The victory lifted Sunrisers to 18 points and, crucially, boosted their net run rate to +0.524.

## Kishan and Klaasen light up Hyderabad

The evening belonged to Ishan Kishan, whose 79 off just 42 balls dismantled RCB's bowling attack with a ferocity that left even Bhuvneshwar Kumar, the tournament's joint-leading wicket-taker, searching for answers. Kishan's innings featured nine fours and four sixes, with his scoring rate accelerating through the middle overs when he took apart the spin of Krunal Pandya and the medium pace of Tim David.

Abhishek Sharma set the tone at the top with a rapid 56 off 30 balls, punishing Rasikh Salam's fuller deliveries through the powerplay. By the time Heinrich Klaasen arrived, SRH were already in command — but the South African ensured there was no let-up, smashing 51 off just 24 balls with five towering sixes. Josh Hazlewood bore the brunt, conceding 22 runs in a single Klaasen-dominated over.

RCB's reply never gained the required momentum. Despite solid contributions from their middle order, the asking rate spiralled beyond reach after the powerplay, and Bengaluru eventually finished on 200/4 — a score that would have been competitive on most nights, but not against SRH's batting avalanche.

## The unprecedented three-way tie

The result means the top three of the IPL 2026 points table reads:

| Position | Team | Points | NRR |
|----------|------|--------|-----|
| 1 | RCB | 18 | +0.783 |
| 2 | GT | 18 | +0.695 |
| 3 | SRH | 18 | +0.524 |

All three have completed their 14 league matches with identical win-loss records of 9-5. RCB's superior net run rate, built during a dominant early-season run that included victories by 43 runs, 23 runs and nine wickets, earns them the top spot and the privilege of playing Qualifier 1 against Gujarat Titans. SRH, despite finishing third, are guaranteed a home Eliminator against whoever claims the fourth spot.

This is the first time in IPL history that three teams have finished on identical points tallies at the summit. In 2014, three teams shared 18 points — but none held the outright top position simultaneously with identical played-won records.

## The fourth-spot scramble

Below the big three, Rajasthan Royals sit fourth on 14 points with one match to play. Punjab Kings (13 points), Kolkata Knight Riders (13 points) and Delhi Capitals (12 points) all retain mathematical chances of overhauling them, but each needs results to fall precisely in their favour.

Saturday's double-header will settle everything. LSG host PBKS in the afternoon fixture — a dead rubber for Lucknow but potentially season-defining for Punjab, who need a win and favourable results elsewhere. The evening match brings KKR against DC at Eden Gardens, a straight shootout where the loser's season is almost certainly over.

For Rajasthan, who have a game against Mumbai Indians on Sunday, the equation is simpler: win and they are through, regardless of other results.

## The NRI viewing calendar

For diaspora fans who have rearranged weekends around IPL scheduling all season, the final three matches offer the most dramatic conclusion in years. Saturday's fixtures begin at 3:30 PM IST (6 AM ET, 11 AM BST), with the decisive evening match at 7:30 PM IST (10 AM ET, 3 PM BST). Sunday's final league match follows the same evening slot.

With three matches remaining and four teams in contention for one playoff berth, the 2026 league stage is heading for the most tense finish since the tournament's inception. The top three are locked in; below them, everything remains to play for.
